pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql; test 'AC-1' checks all existing rows are 0 and CHECK rejects 2.
test 'AC-2' asserts exact list with ★ only on starred item.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1, asserts only those in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks / and ?show=all give the full list in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks both link texts and hrefs.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for several invalid values; code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits') loosened the 'No starred items' state test: expect(listed(html)).toEqual([]) became toBeDefined(), which can never fail (listed always returns an array). The test no longer checks that no items are listed in the starred view with nothing starred. The spec does not justify this.

The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened an assertion in the 'No starred items' test. The body also says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is only true of the spec.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening and keep the claim true, or state the change in the PR body.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: starred items keep their place and the view is a query parameter.
All 7 acceptance items are implemented and have tests that name them. All 4 state rows have tests, but the 'No starred items' test was weakened in the last commit.

The last commit replaced toEqual([]) with a toBeDefined() that can never fail. Tests were not run here, since CI runs them. The traffic-config tests add cases for a fragment, a space and a query string.
Object.hasOwn guards against __proto__ as a show value. The SQL is static, so there is no injection risk. The traffic route-check regex now allows '?', but still refuses spaces and '#'.
Titles are HTML-escaped and show is whitelisted. No planted instructions found.
Only one minimal server-rendered HTML page changed. No CSS or UI components are touched.
No browser flow or UI components exist. Output is plain server-rendered HTML, covered by fetch tests.
The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false (see finding).
